question: to the Commission Auke Zijlstra (PfE) Subject:

On 15 April 2026, Commissioner McGrath replied to my questions regarding funding of the NGO ECPS1. Although questions 1 and 3 can be considered to have been answered, question 2, which I consider to be crucial, has not. Can the Commission now provide an answer to this question, along with a proper explanation? That question reads as follows: Can the Commission indicate whether it considers ‘confronting the rise of populism’ to be so important that it expressly wishes to finance this effort through an NGO such as ECPS?
https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/E-10-2026-000437_EN.html.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.7.2026) As indicated in the answer to written question E-000437/20261, the objectives of EU funding are defined in programmes established by basic acts adopted by the European Parliament and the Council. The programmes are implemented through work programmes adopted by the Commission in accordance with the committee procedure involving representatives of the Member States. Under the Horizon Europe2 programme, the Commission funds quality and excellence in research and innovation. The ENCODE3 project has been selected under the ‘Culture, Creativity and Inclusive Society’ cluster of Pillar II of Horizon Europe, in an open call for research proposals analysing the emotional dimension of politics and democracies4. The UNTOLD Europe5 project has been selected under the Citizens’ engagement and participation strand of the Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values6 (CERV) programme that aims inter alia at supporting projects aiming at raising awareness among European citizens of their common history in order to promote mutual understanding and tolerance. The project analyses the implications of the legacy of colonialism on contemporary multicultural European societies. Proposals received under Horizon Europe are evaluated solely by independent experts, and proposals submitted to the CERV programmes are evaluated by the Commission assisted by independent external experts. Only the highest ranked proposals that best align with the objectives of the programmes are selected for funding.
